items.rationale: Sections 2.4.4 and 7.1.9 cover like-for-like replacement of the internal frost-fractured valve. Case 25 supports €52.50 gross for one valve.
Section 7.1.9 covers connection elements that must be renewed with the valve. Case 25 supports €27 gross for one hose.
Sections 7.1.7(f) and 7.1.9 cover the labour needed to renew the fitting. Three hours at €95 gross gives €285, consistent with Case 25's confirmed lower bound.

Sections 7.1.7(e) and 3.6 distinguish consumables actually used in the covered repair from the contractor's own tools and small equipment. Allow €7 gross for necessary consumables, consistent with Case 25.
Sections 7.1.9 and 7.1.11 cover one attendance for the plumbing undertaking. Case 25 supports €41 gross for that attendance.
Sections 2.4.6 and 5.2.2 expressly cover imaging equipment used to locate the escape. Allow €25 gross for the equipment use, consistent with Case 25 and within the €2,500 gross event limit.
Section 7.1.11 excludes a separate return attendance unless approved in advance, and no approval is stated. If approved, an ordinary vehicle charge would be about €41 gross.

The facade frost endorsement brings removal of failed render on the damaged elevation within sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(a). Allow two removal units at €55 gross each, excluding separately billed disposal.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(d) cover like-for-like base plaster on the damaged area. Allow €65 gross for one material line, without duplicating substrate work or painter labour.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(c) cover reinstating the damaged substrate. Allow €140 gross for local preparation and re-forming, excluding the separately billed base plaster and painter hours.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(d) cover the primer required by the matching finish system on the damaged area. Allow €40 gross for one priming line, apart from separately billed painter labour.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(c) cover drying only where needed before making good the damaged substrate. Allow €85 gross for a modest local drying measure if necessary, not for ordinary waiting time.

Sections 2.6.2, 7.1.7(d) and 7.1.10 limit payment to the coats required by the like-for-like finish system on the damaged area. Allow €135 gross for paint on that basis, excluding the rear elevation and separately billed labour.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(f) cover painter labour attributable to the frost-damaged elevation; section 9.6 requires separation from the rear work. Five covered hours at €66 gross gives €330.

Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.8 cover necessary access for the insured facade work. At about 48 m² and €15 gross per m² for a short hire including erection and dismantling, allow €720 with no rear-work apportionment.
Sections 2.6.3(a), 7.1.5 and 7.1.6 exclude repainting a separate undamaged elevation, including for appearance matching. The €500 gross figure is conditional only; no payment is expected.
Sections 2.6.2 and 5.2.1 cover necessary transport and disposal of render removed from the insured area. Allow €60 gross for a few rubble sacks, not a skip.
Sections 3.6(b) and 7.1.12 exclude an administrative surcharge that prices no repair work. The €10 gross figure is conditional only; no payment is expected.
Sections 3.6(a) and 7.1.12 exclude crew subsistence even when the underlying work is covered. The €6 gross figure for all three units is conditional only; no payment is expected.
